chunks: A woman came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and said, “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, I have committed adultery, so purify me. May Allah purify you, for the punishment of this world is easier than the punishment of the Hereafter, which does not cease.” He said, “From what shall I purify you?” She said, “From adultery.” He said to her, “Are you a woman with a husband or one without a husband?” She said, “A woman with a husband.” He said to her, “Was your husband present or absent?” She said, “Present.” He said, “Wait until you deliver what is in your womb, then come to me.” So when she turned away from him to where she could not hear his words, he said, “O Allah, this is one testimony.”

She did not wait long before she came to him and said, “I have delivered, so purify me.” He acted as though unaware and said to her, “Shall I purify you, O servant of Allah, from what?” She said, “I have indeed committed adultery and have delivered, so purify me.” He said, “Were you a woman with a husband when you did what you did, or were you without a husband?” She said, “Rather, I was a woman with a husband.” He said, “And was your husband absent or present?” She said, “Rather, present.” He said, “Go until you nurse him.” So when she turned away to where she could not hear his words, he said, “O Allah, these are two testimonies.”

When she had nursed him, she returned to him and said, “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, I have committed adultery, so purify me.” He said to her, “Were you a woman with a husband when you did what you did, or without a husband?” She said, “Rather, a woman with a husband.” He said, “And was your husband present or absent?” She said, “Rather, present.” He said, “Go and take care of him until he understands to eat and drink, and does not fall from a roof and does not tumble into a well.” So she turned away weeping, and when she turned to where she could not hear his words, he said, “O Allah, these are three testimonies.”

Then ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth met her while she was weeping and said, “What makes you weep?” She said, “I came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and asked him to purify me, and he said to me: Care for your child until he eats and drinks and does not fall from a roof and does not tumble into a well. I have feared that death may overtake me while he has not purified me.” So ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth said to her, “Return, for I will take care of your child.” So she returned and informed Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام of the statement of ʿAmr. Then Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said to her, “Why should ʿAmr take care of your child?” She said, “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, I have committed adultery, so purify me.” He said, “And were you a woman with a husband when you did what you did?” She said, “Yes.” He said, “And was your husband present or absent?” She said, “Rather, present.”

Then Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام raised his head toward the sky and said, “O Allah, I have established that against her with four testimonies, and You have said to Your Prophet صلوات الله عليه وآله in what You informed him of from Your religion: ‘O Muḥammad, whoever neglects a hadd from among My hudud has indeed opposed Me and contended against Me in My dominion.’ O Allah, and I am not one who neglects Your hudud, nor one seeking to oppose You, nor one contending against You, nor one wasting Your rulings; rather, I am obedient to You, following the sunnah of Your Prophet.”

Then ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth looked at him and said, “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, I only intended to take care of him because I thought that was something you liked; but now that you have disliked it, I will not do it.” Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said, “After four testimonies, by Allah, you shall most certainly take care of him while humbled.” Then he عليه السلام stood, ascended the pulpit, and said, “O Qanbar, call among the people: al-salat jāmiʿah.” So the people gathered until the mosque became full with its people. Then he said, “O people, your Imam is going out with this woman to the open plain to establish the hadd upon her, if Allah wills.” Then he descended.

So when morning came, he went out with the woman, and the people went out disguised and veiled with their turbans, with stones in their hands, cloaks, and sleeves, until they came to the open plain. He ordered that a pit be dug for her, then buried her in it up to her hips. Then he mounted his mule, fixed his foot in the stirrup, then placed his two index fingers in his ears, then called in the loudest of his voice, “O people, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, entrusted His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله with a covenant, and His Prophet entrusted me that no one upon whom there is a hadd due to Allah should carry out the hadd. So whoever has upon him a hadd due to Allah like what is upon her should not carry out the hadd upon her.” So all the people departed that day except Amīr al-Muʾminīn and al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn عليهم السلام, and they carried out the hadd upon her, with no one else from the people being with them.

key_terms.حُدُودِي: My legal limits or prescribed punishments, as stated in the divine address
key_terms.ذَاتُ بَعْلٍ: a married woman, literally one possessing a husband
key_terms.شَهَادَاتٍ: testimonies or repeated attestations establishing the confession
key_terms.فَٱكْفُلِيهِ: to take responsibility for and care for the child
key_terms.ٱلزِّنَا: adultery/fornication, the offense confessed in the report

ai.seo_question: How did Amīr al-Muʾminīn Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام handle a repeated confession of zina when the woman had a child?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates how a woman repeatedly confessed zina before Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, who delayed the legal punishment until her child’s rights were secured through birth, nursing, and care. It highlights the procedural gravity of hudud, the need for repeated confession, and the Imam’s strict adherence to divine legal rulings while safeguarding the welfare of the child.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.5018 - A woman came to the Commander of the Faithful, Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as), and said: "O' Commander of the Faithful, I have committed adultery, so purify me. May Allah (swt) purify you, for the punishment in this world is lighter than the punishment in the Hereafter, which never ends."
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) asked her: "From what should I purify you?"
She replied: "From adultery."
Imam (as) then asked: "Are you a married woman or not?"
She said: "I am married."
Imam (as) asked: "Was your husband present or absent?"
She replied: "He was present."
Imam (as) said: "Wait until you give birth to what is in your womb, then come to me."
As she turned away and could no longer hear him, Imam (as) said: "O' Allah (swt), this is one testimony."

Not long after, she returned and said: "I have given birth. Purify me."
Imam (as) feigned ignorance and said: "Purify you from what, O' servant of Allah (swt)?"
She replied: "I have committed adultery and have given birth, so purify me."
Imam (as) asked her again, "Were you married when you did what you did or not?"
She said: "Yes, I was married."
Imam (as) asked: "Was your husband absent or present?"
She answered: "He was present."
Imam (as) said: "Go and nurse your child."
As she turned away and could no longer hear him, Imam (as) said: "O' Allah (swt), these are two testimonies."

After she had nursed her child, the woman returned to the Commander of the Faithful, Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as), and said: "O' Commander of the Faithful, I have committed adultery, so purify me."
Imam (as) asked her: "Were you married when you did what you did or not?"
She replied: "Yes, I was married."
Imam (as) asked: "Was your husband present or absent?"
She answered, "He was present."
Imam (as) said: "Go and care for your child until he becomes aware enough to eat, drink, not fall from a roof, and not stumble into a well."
The woman turned away weeping, and when she was far enough not to hear him, Imam Ali (as) said: "O' Allah (swt), this is the third testimony."

As she was crying, Amr ibn Hurayth met her and asked: "Why are you crying?"
She replied: "I went to the Commander of the Faithful (as) and asked him to purify me, but he told me to care for my child until he eats, drinks, does not fall from a roof, and does not stumble into a well. I am afraid that death will come to me before I am purified."
Amr ibn Hurayth said to her: "Return, for I will take responsibility for your child."
She returned to Imam Ali (as) and informed him of Amr's offer.
Imam Ali (as) asked her: "Why would Amr take responsibility for your child?"
She said: "O' Commander of the Faithful, I have committed adultery, so purify me."
Imam (as) asked: "Were you married when you committed this act?"
She replied: "Yes."
Imam (as) then asked: "Was your husband present or absent?"
She replied: "He was present."

At this, the Commander of the Faithful, Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as), raised his head toward the sky and said: "O' Allah (swt), I have confirmed this against her with four testimonies. And You (swt) have said to Your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) regarding Your (swt) religion:
'O' Muhammad (sw), whoever abandons one of My (swt) prescribed punishments has opposed Me (swt) and contended with Me (swt) in My (swt) dominion'.
'O' Allah (swt), I do not abandon Your (swt) punishments, nor do I seek to oppose You (swt) or contend with You (swt). I do not neglect Your (swt) rulings but rather obey You (swt) and follow the Sunnah of Your (swt) Prophet."

Amr ibn Hurayth then said: "O' Commander of the Faithful, I only offered to take responsibility for her child because I thought you would like that. But if you dislike it, I will not do it."
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) responded: "After four testimonies by Allah (swt), you will indeed take responsibility for him, and you will do so in humility."
Then Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) stood up, ascended the pulpit, and said: "O' Qanbar, call out among the people that the prayer is gathering."
The people gathered until the mosque was full.
Then Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said: "O' people, your Imam will go out with this woman at noon to carry out the prescribed punishment upon her, God willing."
Then Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) descended from the pulpit.

When the morning came, Imam (as) went out with the woman, and the people followed, disguised and veiled with their turbans, holding stones in their hands, hidden in their cloaks and sleeves. They proceeded until they reached the open area (Al-Zuhr).
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) ordered a pit to be dug for her, and she was buried in it up to her waist.
Imam (as) then mounted his mule, placed his foot firmly in the stirrup, put his index fingers into his ears, and called out in a loud voice:
"O' people! Verily, Allah (swt) the Blessed and Exalted entrusted His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) with a trust, and His Prophet (sw) entrusted me that none should carry out the prescribed punishment except one upon whom there is no prescribed punishment from Allah (swt). Therefore, whoever among you has a punishment upon him from Allah (swt) like the punishment upon her, let him not execute the punishment upon her."
Upon hearing this, all the people left that day, except for the Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) and Imam Hasan ibn Ali (as) and Imam Hussain ibn Ali (as). They alone carried out the prescribed punishment upon her, and none of the people remained with them.
